actions.label: Investigate: Align Quick Accent gaming suppression with its supported policy

reproduce.title: Quick Accent: "Do not activate when Game Mode is on" has no effect
reproduce.version_requirement: Reported game/PowerToys versions and current supported build
prerequisites: Use one affected game and the Game Mode checkbox.
Keep a normal desktop application and an explicitly excluded game as controls.
reproduce.expected_result: The detector result and intended suppression policy explain the behavior without assuming every recognized game returns D3D fullscreen.
steps: Invoke Quick Accent in the affected game using fullscreen and borderless modes separately.
Maintainer instrumentation records SHQueryUserNotificationState status/value for each attempt.
Compare desktop and explicit-exclusion controls; distinguish Game Bar recognition from the notification-state result.

known_information: The report and replies show different behavior across games, including games explicitly excluded as a workaround.
KeyboardListener::IsSuppressedByGameMode uses the shared detect_game_mode helper.
The helper calls SHQueryUserNotificationState and returns true only for QUNS_RUNNING_D3D_FULL_SCREEN; API failure returns false.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and public discussion, current ownership, labels and linked-work history.
Read the game-by-game confirmations and explicit excluded-app workaround.
Inspected PowerAccentKeyboardService/KeyboardListener.cpp and common/utils/game_mode.h, including the precise accepted state and failure behavior.
inferences: Borderless/windowed games or a different Windows gaming classification may not satisfy this detector, explaining why the checkbox can appear ineffective in selected games.
issue_context.summary: Quick Accent Game Mode suppression currently checks a D3D-fullscreen notification state, which is not the same as Game Bar game classification.
issue_context.analysis: The code provides a specific detector mismatch to investigate, not a generic event/state design. First establish the actual notification state and intended supported game policy; a Game Bar recognized game does not automatically imply this API returns fullscreen.

fix_assessment.rationale: This is a scoped, confidence-qualified investigation/fix proposal, not an approved or independently converged implementation design.

judgment.rationale: The code provides a specific detector mismatch to investigate, not a generic event/state design. First establish the actual notification state and intended supported game policy; a Game Bar recognized game does not automatically imply this API returns fullscreen.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce fullscreen versus borderless behavior and decide the supported suppression policy before changing the shared detector.

title: Quick Accent: "Do not activate when Game Mode is on" has no effect

confidence.rationale: The source mismatch is concrete, but the actual returned state and intended broader product policy are not yet established.

plan: Reproduce an affected game in fullscreen and borderless modes while recording the existing helper result.
Define whether this setting promises D3D fullscreen suppression or broader Windows gaming classification; assess other callers before changing the shared helper.
Implement the confirmed policy in the narrowest appropriate boundary and add tests for accepted states, API failure, and explicit excluded apps.
proposed_fixes.title: Align Quick Accent gaming suppression with its supported policy
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The D3D-fullscreen-only notification-state detector may miss games that users consider Game Mode active, particularly borderless/windowed cases.
verification: The intended gaming modes suppress Quick Accent consistently and normal desktop typing remains available.
Explicit application exclusion continues to work; unrelated callers do not silently acquire a broader suppression policy.
